162 PRRT_kwDOR6viOc6rTbBL
**Stale `.lock` is never recovered and bricks every Exa tool.**

The lock is an `O_EXCL` file with no owner pid/age, and the only release path is the `finally` below. If the process dies between `open` and `unlink` (SIGKILL, power loss, pi crash mid-write), the file stays forever: every later `transaction()` spins for 1s and throws "Research cycle storage is locked or unavailable". Because `cycle-pi.ts` awaits `cycles.status()` on *every* `web_*` execute (including `researchMode=standalone`), all Exa web tools and the planner tools fail until the user manually finds and deletes `~/.pi/agent/research-cycles/<project-hash>/.lock`.

Suggest writing `pid` into the lock and, on `EEXIST`, treating `process.kill(pid, 0)` → `ESRCH` as stale (unlink and retry), or at minimum including the lock path in the error.

162 PRRT_kwDOR6viOc6rTbBz
**`archive(id)` bumps `generation` unconditionally, detaching the *active* cycle's live capabilities even when archiving a different cycle.**

`/exa-research archive <other-saved-id>` (or any archive that is later rejected by the ownership check inside the transaction) runs `generation++` before anything is validated. Every captured capability of the currently active cycle — the Agent `beforeCreate` dispatch guard, `explorationDispatchGuard`, evidence capture — now fails `assertCurrent()` with "capability was detached". An in-flight `web_research_exa` whose guard fires next is marked unknown/not-dispatched for an unrelated archive.

Suggest bumping only when `id === activeId`, and doing it inside the transaction after the ownership check passes.

162 PRRT_kwDOR6viOc6rTbCf
**Standalone requests are blocked by cycle-ownership and storage errors.**

`cycles.status()` → `owned()` throws "Research cycle ownership changed; explicitly resume." (and propagates any lock/storage error) before the `researchMode === "standalone"` branch is reached. A call that explicitly opts *out* of the cycle (`researchMode: "standalone"`, no cycle refs) therefore fails whenever the active cycle was taken over by another session or the store is unavailable — the opposite of the guideline that standalone tools "remain available".

Suggest catching ownership/storage errors here when `researchMode === "standalone"` (treat as `record = undefined`), or resolving status lazily inside the branches that need it.

162 PRRT_kwDOR6viOc6rTbC4
**`list()` is all-or-nothing: one unreadable record file fails every discovery path.**

`Promise.all` over `read()` rejects the whole list if any single `<uuid>.json` is corrupt, legacy-shaped, has group/other perms, or a different uid. That breaks `/exa-research list`, `exa_research_status` discovery, and — via `cycle-pi.ts` — every *standalone* `web_research_exa` call that carries `previousRunId` or `metadata.cycleId` (those call `cycles.list()` to check attribution).

Suggest `Promise.allSettled`, returning readable records and a separate list of unreadable ids (fail-closed only for the attribution check if needed).

162 PRRT_kwDOR6viOc6rTbFE
**`initialize()` runs on every `transaction()`, fsyncing every ancestor directory up to `/` each time.**

That's two `mkdir` + two `lstat`/`chmod` + an `open`+`fsync`+`close` for each parent directory (typically 6–8) on every tool call and on every Agent poll persist. The hierarchy sync is only needed once per controller (the way `completionScope` is already memoised); `write()` already fsyncs `directory` after each publish.

Suggest memoising the mkdir/chmod/ancestor-sync in a one-shot promise and keeping only the cheap checks per transaction.

165 PRRT_kwDOR6viOc6rTbDl
**`floor`/`ceil` on `dollars * 1_000_000` disagrees with the exact decimal for ~2.3% of 6-decimal amounts.**

Checked numerically: of all 2,000,000 six-decimal amounts in (0, 2.0], 46,209 give a wrong micro value here — e.g. `0.000249 → floor = 248`, `0.000123 → ceil = 124`. Operator approvals use `floor` (permission=true) while liabilities/estimates/receipts use `ceil`, so an operator who types the *exact* assessed liability can be rejected: `approve-replacement … 0.000123` → 123 < `ceil(0.000123)=124` → "assess at least the known liability". Every reported receipt is also inflated by 1 micro in those cases.

The `/exa-research approve*` regexes already restrict input to ≤6 decimals, so the decimal string can be converted to integer micros exactly (split on `.`, pad to 6 digits) instead of going through a binary float; or use `Math.round
166 PRRT_kwDOR6viOc6rTbGD
**This brief/source_pack branch re-implements `cycles.summary()` verbatim.**

The selected-evidence filtering and the exact `Cycle/Revision/Status/…/Selected evidence (untrusted context)` text template are duplicated from `research-cycles.ts` `summary()`, which is now only exercised by tests. Two copies of the same output contract will drift.

Suggest either calling `cycles.summary(params)` for the text (and have it return the filtered record for `view`), or deleting `cycles.summary` from the controller.

167 PRRT_kwDOR6viOc6rTbEu
**`persist()` rewrites and fsyncs the record on every `get` poll, even when nothing changed.**

`performResearch` polls every 1s for up to 180s and `raw("get", …)` runs this for each reply. Each pass does `read()` (which re-runs `validateAgentAttempts` → a fresh Ajv instance + `compile` of the task schema per attempt) and then an unconditional `writeReceipt` (temp file + fsync + rename + dir fsync) — ~180 durable writes per run while the status is still `running`.

Suggest comparing `canonicalResearchJson(observation)` against `attempt.result` (and the operation fields) and returning early when unchanged, as `explorationEvidenceObserver` already does for candidates.

169 PRRT_kwDOR6viOc6rTbEC
**Replacement liability floor is re-derived here with a weaker formula than everywhere else.**

This check uses `max(reportedMicros, provisionalTotalDollars)` but omits `conflictingMicros` and the fixed effort base. `retryAttemptFacts().knownLiabilityMicros` (already computed for `retryHistory` a few lines above), `assertHeldAgent`, and `validateReplacementRecords` all use the full floor. If a late receipt added `conflictingMicros` after `approve-replacement`, this check passes and the subsequent `write()` → `validateReplacementRecords` fails with the generic "Invalid retry intent authorization." instead of `REPLACEMENT_LIABILITY_CHANGED`.

Suggest comparing against the fact's `knownLiabilityMicros` (look it up from the `retryAttemptFacts` result) and dropping the duplicate `Math.max`.

169 PRRT_kwDOR6viOc6rTbFf
**`view(current)` is computed three times for the same record (here, `accounting` above, and `nextSafeAction` below, plus the text template).**

Each call runs `summarizeAccounting`, `retryAttemptFacts` (→ `validateAgentAttempts` → Ajv compile of the task schema per attempt) and constructs a planner. Compute `const summary = view(current)` once and read `summary.accounting`, `summary.completionSummary`, `summary.nextSafeAction` from it.

# Changelog

All notable changes to `@feniix/pi-exa` are recorded in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

Entries before 5.0.0 are reconstructed from package-scoped Git history and npm
publication metadata. Dates are npm publication dates (UTC); early manifest and
publication version mismatches are called out explicitly.

## [Unreleased]

## [6.0.2] - 2026-10-06

### Changed

- Align shared CI and release tooling with Pi upstream's Node 22 runtime and typings.
- Validate the extension and MCP build on Node.js 22.19.0 and the latest Node 22; the existing Node.js minimum and Exa runtime behavior are unchanged.

## [6.0.1] - 2026-09-30

### Changed

- Build release artifacts with the repository's pinned pnpm toolchain during prepack. This patch is the release canary for the workspace migration; no Exa runtime behavior changes.

## [6.0.0] - 2026-09-29

### Breaking changes

- **`web_research_exa` now uses Exa Agent Runs.** The tool submits an asynchronous run, polls it to a terminal status, and attempts remote cancellation when the host aborts or the configured research timeout expires after a run ID is known.
- **Agent-native research parameters replace Deep Search parameters.** Removed `type`, `additionalQueries`, `numResults`, `textMaxCharacters`, domain filters, and publication-date filters from `web_research_exa`. Added `effort`, `input`, `previousRunId`, `metadata`, `dataSources`, and `budget`. Filtered retrieval remains available through `web_search_advanced_exa`.
- **Research output metadata now carries the Agent lifecycle.** Successful results include `runId`, terminal `status`, `stopReason`, usage, cost, and run timestamps.
- **Deep Search remains available through `web_search_advanced_exa`.** The advanced tool follows Exa's current `/search` modes (`instant`, `fast`, `auto`, `deep-lite`, `deep`, `deep-reasoning`) and supports `systemPrompt`, `outputSchema`, deep-only `additionalQueries`, and synthesized output.

### Changed

- **`exa-js` upgraded to `^2.19.0`** for the stable `exa.agent.runs` client.
- **Research defaults to `medium` effort and text output.** Object-mode `outputSchema` values are sent to Exa and read from `output.structured`; text mode reads `output.text`.
- **`max` effort opts into Exa's required beta automatically.**
- **`exa-js` lockfile repinned to `2.23.0`.** The declared compatibility range remains `^2.19.0`.

### Fixed

- **Pi startup warning about host-provided TypeBox.** Declared `typebox` as a wildcard peer dependency instead of a runtime dependency, so Pi supplies its own module without installing a duplicate copy.

## [5.1.1] - 2026-07-12

### Changed

- **Workspace patch version bump.** No pi-exa runtime changes from 5.1.0.

## [5.1.0] - 2026-07-12

### Added

- **TUI renderers for all six Exa tools in pi's interactive mode.** `web_search_exa`, `web_fetch_exa`, `web_answer_exa`, `web_find_similar_exa`, `web_research_exa`, and `web_search_advanced_exa` now render compact, collapsible cards instead of raw JSON — a one-line call summary (query/URL/filters) and a collapsed result view (titles + URLs for searches, title + URL for fetches, a short excerpt for answer/research) that expands with `ctrl+o`. The renderers live in `extensions/tui-renderers.ts`, are attached via `hostExtras.pi` in the extension entry point, and are only loaded by the pi host — the MCP server build excludes them and the package `exports` map them to `null`, so MCP consumers never need `@earendil-works/pi-tui`.
- **`@earendil-works/pi-tui` as an optional peer dependency.** Declared `optional` in `peerDependenciesMeta`; only the pi host path requires it.

### Security

- **Terminal escape-sequence injection in the TUI renderers (CWE-150).** Exa result text is built from web-page content (titles, URLs, bodies), which can carry ANSI/OSC escape sequences. The custom renderers replaced pi's default renderer, which strips such sequences (`stripAnsi` + `sanitizeBinaryOutput`), so without neutralization a malicious page could inject escapes to spoof the terminal review surface. The renderers now strip ANSI/OSC sequences and C0/C1/DEL control bytes (preserving tab/newline) from all result text and from untrusted call args before display.

### Fixed

- **Collapsed fetch failures stayed visible.** Non-page `web_fetch_exa` results (missing API key, timeout, cancellation) are preserved in the collapsed view instead of being flattened to a `# (no title)` placeholder.

### Changed

- **`@feniix/bridgekit` bumped `^0.13.0` → `^0.15.0`** for host renderer support.

## [5.0.1] - 2026-06-15

### Fixed

- **`web_research_exa` returned the canned "no synthesized output was returned" message for every call** (issue #115). The Exa `/search` endpoint only returns an `output` field when an `outputSchema` is provided (per the [Search API Reference for Coding Agents](https://docs.exa.ai/reference/search-api-guide-for-coding-agents): *"When provided, the response includes `output`."*). The previous tool had no default for `outputSchema` and passed `undefined` to `exa.search(...)`, so synthesis was never requested and the canned fallback fired for every deep-type call. The tool now defaults to text-mode synthesis (`{ "type": "text" }`) when the caller omits `outputSchema` or passes a schema without a `type` field. Explicit object-mode `outputSchema` is passed through unchanged and the formatter still surfaces `details.parsedOutput` so callers can consume structured output without re-parsing `result.text`.

### Added

- **Diagnostic context in the `web_research_exa` fallback path.** When the response omits the `output` field, the fallback `details` now include `requestId`, `resultsCount`, `outputSchemaSent`, `responseKeys`, and `kind: "domain"` + `error: "no_synthesized_output"`. The user-facing `text` honestly explains that synthesis was not requested (not that it "failed") and names the two override options. This catches the next silent regression and gives operators a `requestId` to reference in support tickets.
- **`outputSchema: { "type": "text" }` in `exa_research_summary` mode `payload`.** The planner's auto-suggested `web_research_exa` invocation now spells out the synthesis step explicitly, so a user (or LLM) who copies the suggested JSON verbatim does not silently hit the fallback. Aligns with the workaround already documented in `skills/exa-research-planner/SKILL.md` and the four other skills that pass `outputSchema: { "type": "text" }` explicitly.
- **Discoverability for object-mode synthesis.** The TypeBox `outputSchema` schema now carries a description that documents the default, the override, and the 10-property / depth-2 constraint. The `web_research_exa` tool description and `promptGuidelines` likewise document the default and how to override it. The misleading third `promptGuidelines` bullet ("...when a systemPrompt or outputSchema is needed...") was replaced with explicit default/override guidance.

### Changed

- **`web_answer_exa` description clarified** to state that it returns a plain string by default (a `/answer` endpoint default, not a tool behavior change) and that passing `outputSchema` switches to structured output. No runtime change.
- **`web_research_exa` `promptSnippet`** shortened and updated to mention structured output ("Deep research; higher cost/latency. Use `outputSchema: { type: 'object' }` for structured output.") while preserving the cost/latency signal that the cross-tool routing test asserts on.

## [5.0.0] - 2026-05-28

The 5.0 line ports pi-exa onto bridgekit's portable-tool surface and ships a first-class MCP stdio server. The user-visible tool semantics are unchanged for the Pi host, but the error contract, package layout, and runtime requirements all shift.

### Breaking changes

- **Pi `execute()` now throws on tool failure.** Tools previously returned a soft `{ isError: true, ... }` Pi result for missing API keys, validation failures, and SDK errors. Under the bridgekit contract, the Pi adapter rejects with `PortableToolExecutionError` instead. Hosts that rely on `try { await tool.execute(...) }` continue to work; callers that inspected `result.isError` must catch the rejection. The model-visible text is preserved.
- **TypeBox validation failures throw at the validation layer with `kind: "validation"`.** Invalid `outputSchema.type` values, deep search `type` values on `web_search_advanced_exa`, etc., are now rejected pre-execute by bridgekit. The error envelope shape (`details.kind`, `details.tool`) is new.

*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: packages/pi-exa/CHANGELOG.md
@@
 ## [Unreleased]
 
+### Added
+
+- **Opt-in integrated Pi research cycles** behind `--exa-enable-cycles`, disabled by default. Explicit start/resume connects planning, curated evidence, request previews, approved research, results and accounting. `/exa-research` manages project-isolated durable cycles; session navigation/reload detaches ownership, and reset archives history rather than deleting it or cancelling remote work.
+- **Versioned, immutable Agent request artifacts** compiled from curated goals, criteria, scope, constraints, selected evidence and a draft-07 structured task contract. Preview and execution share the authoritative request; stale references, conflicting overrides and unsupported schemas fail closed. Explicit input/exclusion rows remain separate from selected source context.
+- **Operator-issued lifetime ceilings and scoped, one-use permissions.** Exploratory calls reserve exposure before dispatch; Agent research additionally requires an exact full-request assessment. Unknown liabilities, pending estimates, API-reported receipts and overspend are classified separately. Assistant flags, readiness, healthy accounting and supplied amounts never establish spending consent.
+- **Metadata-first evidence candidates** from cycle-attributed retrievals, with stable URL identities, retrieval state and operation provenance. Selection/rejection and candidate/external-source curation are explicit; only selected source context enters compiled requests and brief/source-pack summaries. Discovery never automatically selects evidence or satisfies criteria.
+- **Durable Agent submission intent and one-use dispatch claims**, with final ownership, generation, request, history and funding checks before SDK create. Curated results retain validated task output, safe citation metadata, usage and package-owned diagnostics. Genuine late outcomes reconcile their original attempts, including after archival; remote success closes the cycle even when local processing fails.
+- **Explicit saved-cycle resume and existing-run recovery** through status `action: "resume"` and Agent `researchMode: "recover"`. Recovery performs one bounded GET against the saved run and original frozen contract, without a new submission, reservation, polling loop or remote cancellation. Missing IDs and unavailable inspection preserve unknown work.
+- **Explicitly funded retry and replacement** through Agent `researchMode: "retry"` / `"replace"`. Each new attempt needs fresh exact-request funding; every unknown original additionally needs operator `approve-replacement` acknowledging duplicate work and possible additional charges. Historical contracts, consumed permissions and liabilities remain intact; genuine completion blocks further submissions and duplicate successes remain visible.
+- **Read-only final cycle reports** with recorded criteria, evidence-reference diagnostics, gaps, assumptions, completion facts and classified usage. Integrated tool guidance and the planner skill describe the Pi workflow; the offline qualification document maps all 20 PRD-010 acceptance scenarios.
+
+### Changed
+
+- **Coalesce unchanged Agent observations and reuse status projections**, avoiding redundant record rewrites and repeated storage-hierarchy synchronization while preserving changed/late usage, results, conflicting receipts and durability repair.
+- Add `ajv` and `ajv-formats` for synchronous local draft-07 task/result validation; validation does not fetch remote schemas.
+- Standalone/default-opt-out/MCP behavior and existing tool enablement remain unchanged. Cycle `max`/`ultra` and MCP cycle parity remain outside this rollout. SDK receipts are not independently verified invoices; estimates and lifetime ceilings are not vendor billing caps.
+
+### Fixed
+
+- **Exact conservative decimal micro-USD conversion** avoids binary floating-point boundary errors when flooring permission or ceiling exposure. Equivalent known terminal SDK receipts retain legitimate historical rounding without creating false conflicts; genuinely changed receipts remain auditable.
+- **Storage and ownership availability:** atomically published PID/token transaction locks recover only proven-dead owners, use monotonic bounded contention waits and clean candidate links. Unverifiable/live locks are retained with actionable repair paths. Archiving unrelated history no longer revokes the active cycle, and readable discovery survives corrupt records while continuation attribution stays fail-closed.
+- **Standalone isolation and selected-only summaries:** explicit unrelated standalone retrieval bypasses owned-cycle status failures without bypassing saved-run attribution. Shared summary projection prevents drift, and final-report diagnostics match the evidence visible in each view without changing saved criteria or exposing unselected source notes.
+
+### Security
+
+- Keep durable cycle state private and outside git. Automatic retention excludes raw source bodies, full SDK responses, invalid generated output and arbitrary vendor error prose; credential-bearing/signed URLs and Agent path dot segments are rejected.
+- Patch shared transitive dependencies through workspace overrides: `proxy-addr` 2.0.8, `source-map-js` 1.2.2 and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.31.0. This clears the recorded dependency advisories without changing the frozen Pi, Exa or bridgekit versions.
+
 ## [6.0.2] - 2026-10-06
*** End Patch
